lessons.title: The Erotic Climate
lessons.summary: Why desire rarely appears in the evening but grows over the day, and which small gestures warm the climate.
lessons.content:
Many couples wait for the perfect evening: time, calm, mood. And wonder why it comes so rarely. But desire seldom appears at the push of a button in the evening. It grows over the day, from many small moments in which you experience yourself as desirable and desired. You could call it the erotic climate.

What warms the climate
Touches in passing: a hand on the neck, the back, the hip, without it having to lead to more.
The long kiss: instead of a quick peck when you greet each other, a kiss that lasts a few seconds. Long enough to really arrive.
Looks: looking at the other when they don't expect it, and showing it.
Compliments: concrete and honest, including about the body. “Those trousers suit you.” “I love how you smell.”
Attention: putting the phone away when the other is talking.

What cools the climate
Constant organising without a break, criticism in front of others, touch only when sex is wanted. If you only get tender when you want something, touch becomes a question that sometimes has to be answered with no. Touch without intention takes away that pressure.

The task
Choose three small gestures to do every day for a week: for example the long kiss when you greet each other, a touch in passing and a compliment. Without expecting it to lead to sex. At the end of the week, talk about what has changed.

For singles
There's an erotic climate on your own too: how you treat your body, what you wear, how you move. The fifth lesson looks at this.
lessons.reflection_question: Which small gesture made the biggest difference this week, for you or for your partner?

lessons.title: Anticipation Through the Day
lessons.summary: How one sentence in the morning can make the whole day crackle, and why anticipation is often half the pleasure.
lessons.content:
Anticipation is an underrated part of desire. If you know something lovely is waiting in the evening, you keep thinking about it during the day, and your body starts to prepare. Many people, especially those with more responsive desire, get in the mood exactly like this: not out of nowhere, but because something was set in motion.

The art of the hint
A hint doesn't give everything away, it makes you curious. A sentence at breakfast: “I've got plans for you tonight.” A look that lasts a little too long. A hand that slips a little lower than usual when you say goodbye. Your partner doesn't know exactly what's coming, only that something is.

Anticipation without pressure
Important: a hint is an invitation, not a promise that has to be kept. If tiredness wins in the evening after all, that's fine. Then you cuddle, or the anticipation moves on to the next day. If anticipation feels like an obligation, it's quickly lost.

The task
On one day this week, each of you sends the other a hint in the morning, as a sentence, a note or a message. No details, just a promise of closeness. In the evening you decide together what becomes of it.
Ideas for the note: “I'm looking forward to your skin tonight.” “Keep the evening free.” “I thought about you earlier, and not in a family-friendly way.”

If you have little time
Anticipation doesn't need a whole evening. Even twenty minutes after the children are in bed can feel like a date if you've been looking forward to it all day.

lessons.title: Rituals Against Routine
lessons.summary: Fixed times for closeness, a bed without phones and dates at home: why planning isn't unromantic.
lessons.content:
“Sex has to be spontaneous” is one of the most stubborn myths. At the start of a relationship much was spontaneous, because being in love pushed everything else aside. In everyday life with work, children and tiredness, everyday life pushes desire aside. Rituals create the space in which spontaneity becomes possible again.

A fixed time, not a fixed routine
Agree on a fixed evening each week that belongs only to you. Important: what you agree on is the time, not sex. You can talk, massage, bathe, kiss, or sleep together. Without pressure for anything in particular to happen. Many couples find that this is exactly what brings desire back.

The bed as your place
Phones, laptops and series in bed are desire killers. If you look at screens side by side in the evening, you fall asleep side by side, not with each other. Try it for a week: phones stay outside the bedroom, an alarm clock replaces the phone.

Dates at home
A date doesn't have to be expensive. Cook together, set the table, put on something nice, put on music. Treat each other as if you had just started dating. Ask each other things you don't yet know about one another.

The task
Choose one ritual and try it for two weeks: the fixed evening, the phone-free bed or a date at home each week. Put the ritual in your calendar, as binding as a doctor's appointment.

If a ritual doesn't fit
Then change it. Rituals should serve you, not the other way round. Some couples prefer a fixed morning, others a midday at the weekend.
lessons.reflection_question: Which ritual really fits your everyday life, and what would you have to leave out for it?

lessons.title: Little Games for In Between
lessons.summary: Code words, secrets and touches under the table: games that make everyday life tingle.
lessons.content:
Playful eroticism keeps a relationship young. It brings lightness and the feeling of sharing a secret. And it hardly takes any time.

The code word
Agree on a harmless word that means something completely different to the two of you: for example “pineapple” for “I want you tonight”. If it comes up at dinner with friends or on the phone, only you two know what it means.

The secret
One of you wears something only the other knows about: special underwear, no underwear at all, a perfume that otherwise only appears in the bedroom. All day long your partner knows about it, and perhaps looks at you a little differently.

Touches nobody sees
A hand on the thigh under the table, a finger stroking the palm while you walk, a whisper in the ear while shopping. Always so that nobody else notices and nobody feels bothered, and only if it feels right for both of you.

The compliment game
Every day a compliment about the body, on a note left where the other will find it: in their wallet, on the mirror, in a jacket pocket.

The task
Choose two games and play them for a week. Feel free to invent your own. Notice how it feels to share a secret.

Limits
Games live from both wanting to play. What feels tingly to one person may feel embarrassing to the other, especially in front of acquaintances or colleagues. Briefly agree beforehand where the limits are.
lessons.reflection_question: Which game made you laugh or crackle the most?

lessons.title: Staying Erotic on Your Own
lessons.summary: Sensuality in your own everyday life: how to stay in touch with yourself, in a relationship or on your own.
lessons.content:
Eroticism isn't only something that happens between two people. It starts with your relationship to yourself: how you perceive your body, how you treat it, how often you allow yourself pleasure. If you're in sensual contact with yourself, you bring that aliveness into a relationship, and if you live alone, you don't have to go without it.

Sensuality in everyday life
The shower: not rushed, but a few minutes with warm water on your skin and a shower gel that smells good.
Clothes: wearing something you feel good in, even on perfectly ordinary days.
Music: a song that moves you, and moving to it, alone in the kitchen.
Food: eating slowly, tasting, smelling. Enjoyment is a skill you can practise.
Touch: putting on lotion as if you were someone you like.

Masturbation as self-care
Touching yourself isn't a substitute for sex with another person, but its own form of closeness to yourself. If you know what you like, you can show it. And if you regularly allow yourself pleasure, you often feel more alive in everyday life too.

The task
This week, plan an hour just for you and your body: a bath, music, candles, lotion, and if you like, the guided body journey below this lesson. Treat it like a date you're looking forward to.

In a relationship
Time with yourself is valuable in a partnership too. It takes nothing away from your partner. Many couples find that their own desire enlivens their shared desire as well.
lessons.reflection_question: When did you last deliberately allow yourself pleasure just for you, and how did it feel?

lessons.title: Quickies
lessons.summary: Fast, spontaneous, anywhere in the flat: why quickies aren't second-class sex.
lessons.content:

lessons.title: A Day Full of Tension
lessons.summary: Teasing all day long, with small tasks, and in the evening you make good on it.
